question: What counts as a provider in Nest?
shortAnswer: Injectable classes (services/repos), custom provider objects (useClass/useValue/useFactory/useExisting), and more.
detailedAnswer: Anything that can be injected. Register in module providers (or export from imported modules).

question: useFactory vs useClass vs useValue — when?
shortAnswer: useValue for constants/mocks; useClass for swappable implementations; useFactory for async/config-dependent construction.
detailedAnswer: Factories enable ConfigService-driven setup. Prefer explicit tokens for interfaces.

question: What is a custom injection token and why use string/symbol tokens?
shortAnswer: Tokens identify providers when you inject interfaces or multiple alike dependencies.
detailedAnswer: TypeScript interfaces disappear at runtime — tokens preserve DI identity. Use symbols/consts to avoid collisions.
example:
export const PAYMENTS = Symbol('PAYMENTS');
@Inject(PAYMENTS) private payments: PaymentsPort

question: Transient vs request vs singleton scope — trade-offs?
shortAnswer: Default singleton is shared; request scope per HTTP request; transient new per injection — scopes affect memory and graph.
detailedAnswer: Request-scoped providers force dependents request-scoped (bubble). Use sparingly for tenancy needs; prefer ALS or explicit params when possible.

question: Debugging: Nest says provider not found at runtime.
shortAnswer: Module didn't register/export/import correctly, or wrong token, or circular dependency needing forwardRef.
detailedAnswer: Read the exact token in the error. Check testing module overrides. Circular DI often needs redesign, not only forwardRef.

question: Lead: provider design for ports-and-adapters in Nest?
shortAnswer: Define port interfaces + tokens; adapters as providers; domain services depend on ports only.
detailedAnswer: Swap infra in tests with useValue mocks. Keep ORM details in adapters. Enforce in code review.
